Candidates often find questions on Proof by Contradiction difficult, and this was no exception.

Even setting up the contradiction was not well done. It should have gone along the lines of ‘assume there is an angle x, 90 180 x   such that cos2 1 cos sin x x x − … ’ but often the domain or inequality was missing or incorrect.
Working with the modulus within the inequality proved very demanding with many choosing to ignore it altogether.
There were some excellent solutions, however, and many candidates showed how adept they are at solving problems.

The most popular routes through this proof were via trigonometric identities producing intermediate lines of an appropriate form. Amongst many acceptable intermediate forms were cos sin 1 x x + … , 2 sin2 sin 2 x x … or ( ) 1 cos 45 2 x −   . When these were reached, most high achieving candidates could then argue the contradiction using the range of the functions sinx and cosx within the domain90 180 x    Pearson Education Limited.
notes.display: The most popular routes through this proof were via trigonometric identities producing intermediate lines of an appropriate form. Amongst many acceptable intermediate forms were $|\cos x + \sin x|\ldots1$, $\sin 2x\ldots\sin^2 2x$ or $|\cos(x-45°)| < \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. When these were reached, most high achieving candidates could then argue the contradiction using the range of the functions sinx and cosx within the domain $90° < x < 180°$
